description:
Mohamad Elmasry, media studies professor at the Doha Institute for Graduate Studies, says Washington understands it will not get much help on ending its war with Iran from China, which wants to keep strong ties with Tehran.

“I think China, while they are being hurt to some extent, is in a much better position than many other global players,” ElMasry told Al Jazeera, adding that Beijing has been able to find “workarounds” to the disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

“More importantly, I don’t think the Chinese are willing to jeopardise the relationship that they have with Iran,” he said.

“They’re not allies per se, but it is a kind of strategic partnership,” he added.

“They see it is an important counterbalance to US hegemony in the region. And I don’t think they are willing to surrender the region to the US and Israel.”

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Students and lecturers across Argentina have taken to the streets in protest against sweeping austerity measures introduced by President Javier Milei, demanding the government implement a university financing law already approved by Congress.

The legislation, which would increase funding for public universities, has not been enacted. The government says fiscal constraints and its commitment to a zero-deficit policy under an International Monetary Fund-backed reform programme make implementation impossible.

Universities warn that budget cuts are already disrupting academic operations, affecting classes and essential services, while educators accuse the government of ignoring legally approved spending frameworks. Students say the changes are threatening access to Argentina’s long-standing tuition-free public university system, a cornerstone of social mobility for decades.
